reason: As written the falsifier is mostly non-discriminating and over budget. (1) prediction_if_false ('fixed-degree presentation gives stable size ~p^delta') contradicts the CDM/Chebotarev-Lang-Weil theorem the idea rests on, so the toy can only fail by revealing a mis-stated theorem or a bug; it cannot reopen KN-OPEN-020. The real uncertainty (does the dichotomy plus the rule-5 certificate close the door; are interval/bit predicates the only escape) is theory, not toy-testable. (2) Random degree<=3 existential presentations are generic: Galois group of f(x,Y) over F_p(x) is S_3/S_n, so |F|/p concentrates on a few Chebotarev values (e.g. 2/3 for a generic cubic). The 'intermediate size' cases are measure-zero (degenerate/low-degree-in-x cases) and 5000 random draws will not sample them; 'no intermediate sizes found' is guaranteed by the sampling design. (3) No null/control arm: no positive control showing the harness CAN see an intermediate size (e.g. {x: x^m=1}, m|p-1, |F|=m~p^delta, needs degree m; interval [0,p^delta]; low-bit predicate), and no matched-random-subset null. (4) 'Minimal presentation degree for |F|~p^delta grows with p' is an asymptotic statement about an unbounded search; three primes spaced x4 (p^(1/3)=20,32,51; p^(1/2)=90,181,362) cannot show growth and 'size<=C' with C unspecified absorbs 20-51. Also the +-4*sqrt(p) window is arbitrary: the Weil constant grows with degree and number of auxiliary variables. (5) Runtime: exact |F| for an existential presentation is a projection; brute force over aux y is O(p^2): measured 1.63 s per 2000 y-values at p=131101 => ~107 s per presentation, 5000 presentations => ~150 CPU-hours, not 8 minutes. With >=2 aux variables or forall quantifiers it is p^2..p^3 per presentation, infeasible at 131101. A vectorised gcd(Y^p-Y,f(x,Y)) via powmod over all x is ~0.1-0.3 s per presentation (k=1 only), so 5000 x 3 primes ~ 25-75 CPU-min: still above the 8 min stated, within 20 only if reduced to ~1500 structured presentations/prime. (6) Scaling to p~2^130: the toy says nothing beyond the theorem (uniform in p, error c(d)*sqrt p << p); the only transferable output is the finite mu-set and the constant c(d), and both are better derived from the Galois-group list than sampled. (7) Side gap in the idea: for B=O(1) the claim B*D^2>=N needs a lower bound on D that CDM does not give (needs separate argument: C^m sums cannot cover N targets unless m grows); for B=mu*p, B>=Theta(N) makes rule 5 trivial. Metric is structural (exact |F|, residual/sqrt p), not wall time: that part is fine. Classification if the dichotomy holds: accounting/relabelling closure (theory), not an advance. novelty_unverified stays.
fix: Redesign as a structural-stability test with controls, k=1 aux variable only, vectorised. (A) Family: f(x,Y)=sum c_ij x^i Y^j, deg_x<=3, deg_Y<=3, c_ij in {-1,0,1}, ENUMERATE structured/degenerate ones (not random): all with <=4 nonzero terms (~ few thousand), plus complements (forall = not exists not) and 2-clause Boolean combos with quadratic-character conditions chi(g(x))=+1. Exact |F|: for each x test gcd(Y^p-Y, f(x,Y))!=1 via vectorised numpy powmod (never the O(p^2) y-loop); verify against brute force on p=8209 for 20 presentations. (B) Null model = Chebotarev prediction: compute Galois group G of f over Q(x) (PARI polgalois on specialisation + discriminant/resolvent) and predicted mu = fraction of g in G with a fixed point; compare |F| with mu*p. Metrics (counted/structural): (i) set M_p={round(|F|/p to 3 digits)} and require M_p identical across p up to the p mod 12 class and drawn from the Chebotarev list {0,1/6,1/3,1/2,2/3,5/6,1,...}; (ii) r=(|F|-mu*p)/sqrt(p), report max|r| per degree class c(d) and check it does not grow with p; (iii) gap statistic: count presentations with C<|F|<p/20 (C=2*deg_x*deg_Y); prediction_if_true: 0 for every prime; prediction_if_false: any nonzero count that persists or grows over p. (C) Primes: 12 primes in 8000..140000 covering p mod 12 in {1,5,7,11}, not 3 spaced primes. (D) Positive controls (harness must flag these as intermediate): subgroup {x:x^m=1} for m~p^(1/3),p^(1/2) -> report min degree m (shows minimal degree ~ |F|, the 'grows with p' datum is obtained by construction, not search); interval [0,floor(p^delta)] and low-bit predicate (non-definable; show they leave the mu-set); matched-size uniformly random subset (null for any 'stable size' signal). (E) Budget: k=1, ~1500 presentations x 12 primes x ~0.15 s ~ 45 CPU-min unsplit; cap to ~600/prime at the 4 largest primes and ~1500 at the small ones to land under 20 CPU-min, and record exact counts of powmod calls as cost, no wall time. (F) Scope statement to attach to result: toy verifies only the CDM statement for 1 free variable, 1 aux variable, degree<=3; it carries to p~2^130 only through the theorem (error c(d)*sqrt p, c independent of p), and does not address interval/bit/lattice bases, which remain the sole door. Separately write the B=O(1) case argument (C^m<N for m<log N / log C) so rule 5 is not claimed from CDM alone.
